context.current_question: I am an international applicant interested in the Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering. Is it available to international applicants?
So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?

definitions.E8:
Yes. The full-time Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering is available to international applicants.

Study-permit requirements are not published in the program record and should be confirmed with BCIT International. The program is listed as eligible for graduates to apply for a post-graduation work permit, but approval is not guaranteed.

[View the BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.
definitions.E5:
No. International availability means you’re eligible to apply; it does **not** guarantee admission.

Admission is competitive. Your academic requirements have not been assessed here, and BCIT must confirm your approved Grade 12 course, Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire, complete records, and competitive ranking.

[View the program’s admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
definitions.E3:
I can verify the program’s published academic requirements, but not an admission decision.

**Verified program facts**
- Initial admission requires high-school graduation and at least 73% in Category 1 English, Pre-Calculus 12, Chemistry 11, Physics 12, and one approved Grade 12 academic course—or accepted equivalents.
- Selection also requires the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire and competitive departmental ranking.
- Successful completion of the first two academic years awards the Civil Engineering Diploma.
- Continuing to Level 5 requires the diploma, **CHEM 6020 – Chemistry for Civil Engineering**, **MATH 6010 – Advanced Mathematics for Civil Engineering 1**, a minimum 70% continuation GPA, and 300 practical-work hours. Level 7 requires at least 700 total relevant practical-work hours.

**Confirm directly with BCIT**
- Whether your international courses and credentials satisfy each Canadian subject requirement.
- Whether your additional Grade 12 course is approved.
- Document completeness, questionnaire assessment, and competitive ranking.
- Study-permit requirements and your final admission decision.

[BCIT program and admission information](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/)
definitions.E6: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
definitions.E1: A minimum 70% continuation GPA is required for continuation into Level 5. The continuation GPA is calculated using first-attempt grades from Levels 2, 3 and 4, according to the current BCIT program requirements.
definitions.E2: Competitive initial admission requires high-school graduation, Category 1 English, specified mathematics and sciences, one approved Grade 12 academic course, and the Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire. Departmental ranking is a human institutional decision. Level 5 continuation is not an admission condition in this rule set.
